newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Cargolux calls for integrated air freight system.
newsitem.headline: Cargolux calls for integrated air freight system.

text.p: Cargo airline Cargolux called on Tuesday for an integrated air freight system made up of airlines, forwarders and ground handlers.

Robert Arendal, Senior Vice President of Sales, Marketing and Cargo Services for the Luxembourg-based airline said such a system would focus on the needs of shippers in a coordinated and low-cost environment.
"An integrated air freight system can be made up of airlines, forwarders and ground handlers," he said.

"Air cargo today is not always a user-friendly product. We have more inefficiency and bureaucracy than we want. We have high costs because we lack coordination. Airlines and forwarders often fail to pool technology and infrastructures for their mutual benefit," Arendal told an air cargo conference in this western Swedish city.

He called for sharing of elecronic data to build confidence between airlines and forwarders. "Trust is important because the changing cycle of excess demand and excess capacity makes it difficult for airlines and forwarder to work smoothly together."
"The lack of predictability creates frustration and anger as both sides try to negotiate with each other for the best rates and service," he added.
He said Asian combination passenger-cargo airlines were adding capacity and undermining load factors: "Consequently we are seeing yields in this region decline every year."
"Faced with low yields and a need to buy new aircraft, airlines are well advised to cooperate with forwarders," Arendal said.

Arendal said he had been encouraged at last week's Dubai International Air Cargo Forum, "if only because shippers, forwarders and airlines met together for the first time to discuss the industry's problems."
The only way to provide seamless service for air cargo customers was through greater cooperation between all parties involved in the shipment.
